answers.answer: Each player chooses a color and places that color's Player ID card visibly in front of them. Give each player the Voting card set with that color on its backs; remove cards targeting colors not in play and keep the player's own Ambush card. Deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center with values hidden.
answers.evidence: Setup: “stands its Player ID card visibly in front”; “Remove cards targeting colors that are not playing. Keep your own Ambush card”; “Deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center; keep their values hidden.”

answers.answer: There is no player-by-player voting turn order. A player may change their chosen card until cards are revealed. Once everyone has chosen, all choices are revealed simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “There is no individual turn order.” Vote: “You may change your chosen card until cards are revealed” and “reveal all choices simultaneously.”

answers.answer: No four-vote majority is necessary. The player or players receiving the most votes are Targets, so Red is the sole Target with three votes while Blue and Green each have two.
answers.evidence: Vote: “The player receiving the most votes is the Target. If several players tie for the most votes, all of them are Targets.”

answers.answer: Red and Blue are both Targets because they tie for the most votes; with neither protected by a successful Ambush, both are eliminated. A player who voted for either tied Target satisfies the voting requirement and may survive, subject to the other elimination rules and any Ambush effects.
answers.evidence: Vote: “If several players tie for the most votes, all of them are Targets”; “Each Target is eliminated unless protected by its own successful Ambush”; with tied Targets, “voting for any one of them satisfies the voting requirement.”

answers.answer: No. Green is eliminated: Green did not vote for the sole Target, Blue, and did not successfully Ambush. Receiving no votes does not keep Green alive.
answers.evidence: Vote: “Every other player who did not vote for any Target is also eliminated, subject to the successful Ambush exception below.”

answers.answer: Red's Ambush card adds no vote. Yellow's vote for Red and Pink's vote for Yellow each count as one, so Red and Yellow tie at one vote and both are Targets. Yellow is eliminated; Red's successful Ambush lets Red eliminate one player who voted for Red, so Red eliminates Yellow. Pink voted for a tied Target, Yellow, and survives. Red and Pink survive.
answers.evidence: Three-player illustration: “Red plays Ambush, Yellow votes for Red, and Pink votes for Yellow. Red and Yellow tie at one vote each and are both Targets. Yellow is eliminated; Red survives ... Pink voted for tied Target Yellow and survives, leaving Red and Pink.”

answers.answer: No. A successful Ambush lets the Target eliminate exactly one player who voted for the ambusher. They cannot eliminate all four voters, and they cannot choose someone who voted for another color instead.
answers.evidence: Ambush: “chooses one of the players who voted for them to eliminate. They cannot choose an arbitrary player or someone who voted for a different Target.”

answers.answer: The player eliminates themselves. An Ambush only works if its player is a Target in that vote.
answers.evidence: Ambush: “An Ambush played by someone who is not a Target fails: that player eliminates themselves.”

answers.answer: No gold is awarded yet. With four survivors, continue with another conspiracy and vote among the surviving players; only survivors participate in that subsequent vote.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “Three or more | Continue with another conspiracy and vote among survivors.”

answers.answer: The sole survivor collects all four central Gold Bar cards. They are four cards, not four points; each card is worth 3, 4, or 5 points.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “One | That survivor collects all four central Gold Bars.” Components: “receiving one bar means receiving one card whose value is 3, 4, or 5 points.”

answers.answer: They resolve a Final Showdown for the central Gold Bars. Each takes a set containing Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go. They may discuss intentions and a bargain; each chooses one of the three cards face down, and when both are ready they reveal simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: “each takes a set containing Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go”; they “may discuss their intentions and a bargain,” choose “face down,” and “reveal both choices simultaneously.”

answers.answer: Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. Players who participated in that final vote receive no consolation bar for this outcome. Nobody takes the four central bars; leave them for the next round and add no new bars. If play continues, refill the central pool to four as needed, keeping the bars left behind.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Leave the four central bars for the next round; add no new bars.” The round rules say to refill to four as needed and leave bars explicitly behind.

answers.answer: Each finalist receives two Gold Bar cards.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share versus Share: “You get 2; opponent gets 2.”

answers.answer: The Share player receives zero central bars, and the Steal player receives all four.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share versus Steal: “You get 0; opponent gets 4.”

answers.answer: The Grab One & Go player receives one bar and the Steal player receives the other three.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Grab One & Go versus Steal: “You get 1; opponent gets 3.”

answers.answer: The Grab One & Go player receives one bar and the Share player receives the other three.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Grab One & Go versus Share: “You get 1; opponent gets 3.”

answers.answer: Each finalist takes one central bar; two remain in the center. If play continues, add just two new bars for the next round.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table and rule: “Each gets 1; leave the other 2 in the center”; “add just two new bars for the next round.”

answers.answer: Neither finalist receives gold. Every other player receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round and add no new gold to the central pool.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: “If both choose Steal, neither finalist receives gold. Leave all four central bars for the next round, and give every other player one Gold Bar from the deck. Add no new gold to the central pool.”

answers.answer: Victory is checked at the end of a round, after Gold Bars have been awarded. With 6–9 players, the threshold is at least 25 points; with 10–12 players, it is at least 24 points. If multiple players qualify with different totals, the player with the highest point total wins.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: “at the end of a round, after Gold Bars have been awarded”; “With 6–9 players, reach at least 25 points”; “With 10–12 players, reach at least 24 points”; “If more than one player has reached the threshold, the highest point total wins.”

answers.answer: The tied leaders conduct another Final Showdown; repeat Showdowns as necessary until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest gold point total. After a normal round ends without a winner, everyone returns: stand all Player ID cards upright and begin another round, including players eliminated earlier in the round.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: “the tied players conduct another Final Showdown” and “Repeat these Showdowns as necessary until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest gold point total.” Turn Structure: “If there is no winner, everyone returns: stand all Player ID cards upright and begin another round.”
